etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English serenyte, from Old French serenité, from Latin serēnitās, equivalent to serene +‎ -ity.

definitions.definition: The state of being serene; calmness; peacefulness.

quote.citation: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I, page 193:
quote.text: Forthwith a change came over the waters, and the serenity became less brilliant but more profound.

quote.citation: 1987, Greg Costikyan, “The Jedi Code”, in Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, page 69, line 3:
quote.text: There is no passion, there is serenity.

definitions.definition: A lack of agitation or disturbance.
A title given to a reigning prince or similar dignitary.
